Empirical Research Plan  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Method: Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (FRD) around the exam-school admission cut-offs (one cut-off per school × entry-grade × cohort).  

Why appropriate  
• Assignment to the high-achieving peer environment is a discontinuous (though not perfectly deterministic) function of an explicit running variable – the admission index (Boston composite or NYC SHSAT score).  
• Applicants cannot precisely manipulate the cut-off ex-ante; consequently, just-above and just-below students are plausibly comparable in all unobservables except the large jump in the likelihood of attending an exam school.  
• The FRD can be implemented as a two-stage least squares (2SLS) where the cut-off indicator instruments for actual enrollment, yielding a Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) for “marginal admits.”

Optional extensions  
• Combine RDD with cohort and school fixed effects for stacked FRD.  
• Estimate peer-composition effects directly by using the predicted change in peer mean test score or minority share as the endogenous regressor instead of a simple exam-school dummy.  

================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Running variable  
Boston: School-specific composite index = 0.5 × (standardized GPA) + 0.5 × (standardized ISEE);  
NYC: Raw SHSAT score.  

Cut-off  
For each entry cohort c, school s, and entry grade g, cut-off_{scg} = lowest score offered a seat. This value is known from administrative files.  

Treatment definition  
Ti = 1 if student i actually enrolls in the target exam school in grade 7 (Boston) or grade 9 (Boston & NYC).  

Instrument  
Zi = 1{score_i ≥ cut-off_{scg}}.  

Control group  
Applicants with scores just below the same cut-off who, absent admission, enroll in regular BPS/NYC public schools.  

Treatment timing / event date  
“Exposure” starts the fall following the admission decision (grade 7 or 9) and lasts through secondary schooling; outcomes measured contemporaneously for test scores and several years later for college outcomes.  

================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes: In the absence of treatment, mean potential outcomes vary smoothly with the running variable at the cut-off.  
– Plausible because test prep cannot target an unknown, cohort-specific threshold with the precision of a few points.  

A2. No precise manipulation of the running variable: Density of the score is continuous at the cut-off.  
– Both exams are high-stakes but scored by computer/central offices; retaking is impossible (SHSAT) or costly/time-separated (ISEE).  

A3. First-stage relevance: Being above the cut-off causes a large, discontinuous jump in exam-school enrollment.  
– Confirmable empirically; historical first-stage jump ≈ 0.8.  

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): One student’s potential outcome is not affected by the treatment status of another except through peer composition captured by Ti.  
– Reasonable for FRD local to the margin, though peer-based interference across cohorts is minimal.  

A5. Monotonicity: No applicants who are below the cut-off attend the exam school while some above choose not to; direction of effect is weakly monotone.  
– Holds given admissions policy, except for voluntary no-shows, which only attenuate estimates.  

================================================================  
4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
T1. Manipulation of running variable (score-heaping, cheating, strategic absences).  
  • McCrary density test; visual histogram checks.  
  • Drop cohorts/schools if suspicious spikes emerge.  

T2. Selection into take-up (some admitted students decline the seat; some below the cut-off attend via wait-list).  
  • Use FRD 2SLS to recover LATE among compliers.  
  • Show robustness to definitions of enrollment (e.g., ever attended, attended ≥ 2 years).  

T3. Differential attrition or missing outcome data (e.g., movers leave the data system).  
  • Check balance in attrition rates across cut-off.  
  • Re-code missing outcomes as zeros / use Lee bounds as robustness.  

================================================================  
5. R Code Outline  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# -------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # regressions
library(rdrobust)    # RD bandwidth and inference
library(ggplot2)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load Data (assume CSVs already de-identified and merged)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
boston <- fread("boston_exam_applicants.csv")   # one row per applicant
nyc    <- fread("nyc_exam_applicants.csv")

# stack and keep necessary vars
dat <- rbindlist(list(boston, nyc), fill = TRUE)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct Running Variable, Cut-off, and RD Variables
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# cutoffs pre-computed elsewhere and merged in:
# cutoff_score is school-cohort-specific
dat[, score_minus_cut := exam_score - cutoff_score]      # running variable centered
dat[, Z := (score_minus_cut >= 0)]                       # indicator for above cut-off
dat[, T := enrolled_exam_school]                         # realised treatment

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Outcome Variables
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Example: 10th-grade MCAS/Regents z-score
#          SAT composite z-score
#          College selective_enroll indicator

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Main Fuzzy RD Specification (2SLS local polynomial)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
bw <- 15   # score points; can be optimized with rdrobust

# restrict to symmetric bandwidth
sample <- dat[abs(score_minus_cut) <= bw]

# demean covariates optional
feols(mcas10 ~  Z + poly(score_minus_cut, 2) | 
             0 | (T ~ Z) , data = sample)

# The syntax above performs 2SLS inside fixest (iv = c(T ~ Z)).

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Robustness Check: Different Bandwidth & covariate balance
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Bandwidth 10
sample10 <- dat[abs(score_minus_cut) <= 10]
est10 <- feols(mcas10 ~ Z + poly(score_minus_cut, 2) | 0 | (T ~ Z),
               data = sample10)

# Covariate balance: percent female
cov_bal <- feols(female ~ Z + poly(score_minus_cut, 2),
                 data = sample[bw])

# McCrary density test
rdensity <- rddensity(X = dat$score_minus_cut, c = 0)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot first stage
# -------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(sample, aes(x = score_minus_cut, y = T)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  xlab("Score minus cut-off") + ylab("Enroll in Exam School")
```

================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Economic priors are ambiguous. Peer effects could raise achievement through higher standards and networks, but curriculum pacing and relative-ranking effects could offset gains. My prior:  
• Short-run test scores (state exams) – small positive (≈ 0.05 σ) or zero.  
• SAT/college going – modest positive effect on SAT (≈ 0.08 σ) and probability of 4-year college (≈ 3 pp), with larger gains in college quality (selectivity index +0.1 σ).  

================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
C1: Density continuity at cut-off ………………… 1  
C2: Balance in baseline covariates ……………… 1  
C3: Large first stage (jump in take-up) ……… 1  
C4: Robustness to bandwidth/polynomial ……… 1  
C5: External validity beyond compliers ……… 0   (local LATE only)  

Total = 4 / 5.
